question.question: In a two-Spirit game with 7 of 8 Fear markers already generated, an effect generates 3 Fear and earning a card exposes Terror II. Explain marker handling, new Terror timing, and when the card is revealed/resolved.

fixed_key.answer: Move the eighth marker to earn the top Fear card face-down, reset all 8 to the pool and put the remaining 2 generated Fear toward the next card. Terror II applies as soon as exposed (subject to outcome check at action-tree end). Keep card hidden until Fear step, resolving in earned order at the then-current Terror level only.

question.question: A land with existing Blight has two Presence from Spirit A and one from Spirit B. One new Blight is added after setup. Describe Presence losses, cascade choices and what happens if the cascade enters another already-Blighted land.

fixed_key.answer: Destroy one Presence each of A and B, putting destroyed disks beside the island, not on tracks. Add the original Blight and cascade one additional Blight to one adjacent land, not all. If that land already has Blight it too loses one Presence per Spirit there and cascades again. Existing amount of Blight does not multiply the one cascade.

question.question: Explain gaining a new Minor or Major Power, including how many are drawn, where kept/unkept cards go, Major Forgetting options and the consequences of Forgetting a card already in play.

fixed_key.answer: Choose Minor or Major, draw 4 from that deck, reshuffling its discard if needed; keep one in hand, discard the other three to its deck discard. Gaining a Major requires Forgetting any one owned card (hand, personal discard, in play, even new Major); forgotten Minor/Major goes to its deck discard, Unique under panel. Forgetting in-play immediately loses Elements and unused use; previously resolved effects persist for their normal duration.

question.question: How do Damage, Destroy, Remove and Replace differ for Fear and survival? Can Damage from separate normal Powers combine, does Damage normally hurt Dahan, and does replacement erase prior Damage?

fixed_key.answer: Damage normally means to Invaders only, distributed as chosen in target land; can combine within turn, immediately destroying pieces at Damage >= Health. Destroying Town/City produces 1/2 Fear in addition to explicit Fear. Remove/Replace generate none automatically; Replace retains prior Damage and may cause destruction if Damage meets new Health (then destruction Fear applies). Surviving Damage clears at Time Passes. Dahan are harmed by Powers only if explicitly stated. An outright Destroy instruction eliminates its specified piece regardless of its Damage or Health. Remove likewise takes the specified piece off the board without requiring Damage to reach Health. Replace removes the original and puts the specified replacement in its place.
